title: Images and lifts of Borel subgroups and maximal tori under quotients
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. All groups are affine $F$-group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and subgroups are closed subgroup schemes [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. Smoothness and connectedness have the meanings of [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme]. Write $\mathbf G_a$ and $\mathbf G_m$ for [def-sc-gm-ga]. Faithfully flat means that extension of scalars along the coordinate-algebra map is exact and detects zero modules. Solvable means that the successive scheme-theoretic derived subgroups eventually become trivial; the derived subgroup is the smallest closed subgroup through which the commutator morphism factors. A torus means a group isomorphic to $\mathbf G_m^r$, $r\geq0$; a maximal torus is maximal under inclusion. A Borel subgroup means a maximal smooth connected solvable subgroup. Let $f:A\to D$ be a faithfully flat homomorphism between smooth connected groups. For every Borel subgroup $B\subseteq A$, its scheme-theoretic image $f(B)$ is a Borel subgroup of $D$, and $B\to f(B)$ is faithfully flat. Every Borel subgroup of $D$ is such an image. For every maximal torus $T\subseteq A$, its scheme-theoretic image $f(T)$ is a maximal torus of $D$, and $T\to f(T)$ is faithfully flat. Every maximal torus of $D$ is such an image. No restriction is placed on $\ker f$.

source.place: Proposition 17.20 and its proof, printed pp.357--358, Borel and maximal-torus clauses; Theorem 5.39, printed p.108, for faithfully flat image factorizations.

proof.text: For every restriction of $f$ considered below, with codomain $D$ or an already constructed closed image, [lem-sfb-affine-homomorphism-flat-image] supplies a factorization $J\twoheadrightarrow I\hookrightarrow D$ with the first map faithfully flat. This factor is the scheme-theoretic image: the coordinate algebra of $I$ injects into that of $J$ by [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-universally-injective] applied to the module $F[I]$; hence the kernel of $F[D]\to F[J]$ is exactly the defining ideal of $I$. In particular all the asserted restrictions onto images are faithfully flat. For a Borel $B$ put $C=f(B)$. Apply [lem-sfb-solvable-normal-image-geometry] to the faithfully flat map $B\to C$ with its normal subgroup $N=B$ and image $I=C$. Its hypotheses require normality only inside $B$, which holds for $B$ itself. Thus $C$ is smooth, connected and solvable.

source.place: Theorem 5.39 and Remark 5.42, p.108; Proposition 17.20, p.357, connected and solvable image argument.

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-algebraic-group-homogeneous-quotient] to form the separated finite-type quotients $X=A/B$ and $Y=D/C$. The morphism $A\to D\to Y$ is invariant under right multiplication by $B$: locally it sends $ab$ and $a$ to the same coset because $f(b)\in C$. The quotient kernel-pair formula and [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent] therefore descend this map to $\bar f:X\to Y$. It is surjective: for any geometric point of $Y$, first lift fpqc locally to $D$ and then along the faithfully flat map $A\to D$; composition gives a local lift to $X$. Nonemptiness of the necessary base changes follows from [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-surjective-spectrum]. The scheme $X$ is proper by [lem-sfb-borel-quotient-proper-geometry]. Consequently [lem-weil-pbc-image-universally-closed] makes $Y$ proper, since $Y$ is separated and of finite type.

source.place: Proposition 17.20, p.357, first paragraph; Proposition 5.21, pp.103--104, quotient universal property; A.75(d), descent of completeness under a surjection.

proof.text: Here is the criterion of Proposition 17.19 in the case needed. Choose a smooth connected solvable subgroup $E$ of $D$ of largest dimension; the trivial subgroup starts the nonempty collection. By [lem-sfb-solvable-normal-subgroup-products], dimensions are bounded nonnegative integers and a proper inclusion of smooth connected groups strictly increases dimension. Thus $E$ is Borel. Left multiplication of $D$ on itself descends to an action on $Y=D/C$ by the quotient kernel-pair formula and [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent]; both action identities can be checked after lifting a quotient section. The proper nonempty finite-type scheme $Y$ has an $E$-fixed point by [lem-sfb-solvable-proper-fixed-point]. This point is represented by $d\in D(F)$: lift the point fpqc locally using the quotient statement and then take a closed point in its nonempty finite-type fibre; [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-residue-field-base] identifies its residue field with $F$. The quotient equality criterion says, on every $F$-algebra $R$, that $d_R^{-1}E(R)d_R\subseteq C(R)$. Thus $d^{-1}Ed\subseteq C$ as subgroup schemes. Since $C$ is smooth connected solvable, maximality of the Borel $d^{-1}Ed$ gives $C=d^{-1}Ed$. This proves that every Borel image is Borel without changing the kernel hypotheses.

source.place: Propositions 17.19 and 17.20, p.357; Theorem 17.3 (Borel fixed point), pp.351--352.

proof.text: Choose one Borel $B_0$ of $A$ by the existence argument of step 3. Its image $C_0$ is Borel by steps 1--3. Apply [lem-sfb-algebraic-group-homogeneous-quotient] and [lem-sfb-borel-quotient-proper-geometry] to form the proper $D/C_0$. As in step 3, left multiplication descends to this quotient. By [lem-sfb-solvable-proper-fixed-point], the target Borel $C_1$ fixes a point $dC_0$. The same fibre and residue-field argument gives $d\in D(F)$. Fixedness over every algebra gives $d^{-1}C_1d\subseteq C_0$; Borel maximality makes this equality, so $C_1=dC_0d^{-1}$. Since $D$ is smooth, [lem-sfb-affine-group-homomorphism-image] applied to the given faithfully flat $f$ supplies $a\in A(F)$ with $f(a)=d$. Conjugation is a group-scheme automorphism, so $aB_0a^{-1}$ is again maximal smooth connected solvable. The identity $f(a_R b a_R^{-1})=d_R f(b)d_R^{-1}$ after every scalar extension identifies its scheme-theoretic image with $C_1$. Faithful flatness of the restriction follows from step 1.

source.place: Proposition 17.20, p.358, conjugation and lifting of Borel subgroups; Theorem 17.9(b), p.354.

proof.text: Let $T$ be maximal in $A$. Choose a smooth connected solvable subgroup containing $T$ of largest dimension, starting with $T$ itself (a torus is commutative). The dimension bounds and strict increase in [lem-sfb-solvable-normal-subgroup-products] make it a Borel $B$. Then $T$ is maximal in $B$. Put $C=f(B)$, a Borel by steps 1--3. Since $F$ is algebraically closed it is perfect. Apply [lem-sfb-perfect-solvable-unipotent-torus] to $B$ to obtain a smooth connected normal unipotent $U$ with torus quotient $P=B/U$. By [lem-sfb-solvable-torus-complements], $T\to P$ is an isomorphism. Form the image $V=f(U)\subseteq C$ by step 1. Apply [lem-sfb-unipotent-normal-quotient-image] to $B\to C$ and $U$: $V$ is smooth connected normal unipotent. The quotient $R=C/V$ is affine finite type and smooth connected by [lem-sfb-affine-normal-quotient-geometry]. Since $U$ maps to $V$, the quotient universal properties induce $g:P\to R$. The maps $B\to C$ and $C\to R$ are surjective on $F$-points by [lem-sfb-affine-group-homomorphism-image]. Thus $g$ is surjective on $F$-points (lift a point of $R$ to $B$ and then take its class in $P$). As $R$ is smooth, that node also makes $g$ faithfully flat. Apply [lem-sfb-torus-homomorphism-image] with source $P$, target $R$, image $I=R$ and closed immersion $\mathrm{id}_R$: $R$ is a torus. This uses no reducedness of any kernel.

source.place: Proposition 17.20, pp.357--358, maximal-torus paragraph; Theorem 16.33, p.336; quotient unipotence and torus quotients, Corollary 14.7, p.282, and Definition 12.14, p.236.

proof.text: Let $S=f(T)\subseteq C$, with faithfully flat restriction as in step 1. It is a torus by [lem-sfb-torus-homomorphism-image]. Tori are smooth and connected, so by the dimension bounds and strict increase in [lem-sfb-solvable-normal-subgroup-products] a torus subgroup of $C$ containing $S$ of largest dimension is a maximal torus $S_1$ of $C$ containing $S$. Apply [lem-sfb-solvable-torus-complements] to $(C,V,R)$ from step 5: the restriction $S_1\to R$ is an isomorphism. The composite $T\xrightarrow{\sim}P\xrightarrow{g}R$ is surjective on $F$-points by step 5; it is the restriction to $T$ of $B\to C\to R$, so it factors through $S\subseteq S_1\xrightarrow{\sim}R$, and $S(F)\to S_1(F)$ is surjective. Since $S_1$ is smooth, [lem-sfb-affine-group-homomorphism-image] makes the inclusion $S\hookrightarrow S_1$ faithfully flat. Its coordinate-algebra map is surjective by the affine characterization of [def-weil-closed-immersion] and injective by [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-universally-injective]; hence $S=S_1$. Now $C$ is a Borel subgroup of $D$, so by [lem-sfb-borel-maximal-torus-conjugacy] for $D$ it contains a torus $S'$ maximal in $D$; $S'$ is a fortiori maximal in $C$. The conjugacy clause of the same node for the smooth connected group $C$ gives $c\in C(F)$ with $S=cS'c^{-1}$. Conjugation by $c$ is an automorphism of $D$ preserving inclusions of tori, so $f(T)=S$ is maximal in $D$.

source.place: Proposition 17.20, pp.357--358, conclusion of the maximal-torus paragraph; Theorem 16.33(d), p.336; Theorem 17.10, pp.354--355, and the paragraph after Definition 17.12, p.355.

proof.text: Choose a maximal torus $T_0$ of $A$: by [lem-sfb-solvable-normal-subgroup-products] a torus subgroup of $A$ of largest dimension exists (the trivial torus is one) and, tori being smooth connected, it is maximal. Step 6 makes $S_0=f(T_0)$ maximal in $D$. For any maximal torus $S_2$ of $D$, the conjugacy clause of [lem-sfb-borel-maximal-torus-conjugacy] for $D$ gives $d\in D(F)$ with $S_2=dS_0d^{-1}$. Lift $d$ to $a\in A(F)$ by [lem-sfb-affine-group-homomorphism-image], since $f$ is faithfully flat and $D$ is smooth. Then $aT_0a^{-1}$ is maximal, as conjugation and its inverse preserve inclusions of tori. For every $F$-algebra $R$ the identity $f(a_R t a_R^{-1})=d_Rf(t)d_R^{-1}$ identifies its image subgroup scheme with $S_2$. The restriction is faithfully flat by step 1. Together with step 4 this proves both image-surjectivity clauses, including rank zero.
